title: DNA and other naturally occurring polymers

notes.definition: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) is a large molecule essential for life that encodes genetic instructions. Most DNA molecules are two polymer chains, made from four different monomers called nucleotides, twisted into a double helix. Other naturally occurring polymers important for life include proteins (from amino acids), and starch and cellulose (from sugars).
explanation: Polymers are not only made in factories: living things make many natural polymers, which are essential for life. Like synthetic polymers, they are very large molecules made of many small monomer units joined in long chains. The most important natural polymers are DNA, proteins, starch and cellulose. You need to know which type of monomer each one is made from.

DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) is a large molecule essential for life. It encodes the genetic instructions for the development and functioning of living organisms and viruses. Most DNA molecules are made of two polymer chains twisted around each other in the form of a double helix. Each chain is a polymer made from four different monomers called nucleotides. The order of the different nucleotides along the chain acts as a code: it carries the instructions that the cell uses to make proteins.

Proteins are polymers made from amino acids. Different amino acids are joined together in the same chain by condensation polymerisation, and the order of the amino acids decides the shape and job of each protein. Proteins include enzymes, which catalyse reactions in cells, haemoglobin, which carries oxygen, and structural proteins such as keratin in hair and collagen in skin.

Starch and cellulose are both polymers made from sugar monomers (glucose). Plants make glucose by photosynthesis and join many glucose molecules together. Starch is used by plants as an energy store; it is found in potatoes, rice and bread. Cellulose forms plant cell walls and gives plants strength; cotton and paper are mainly cellulose. Although both are made of glucose, the units are joined differently, so starch and cellulose have different properties.

To summarise the monomers: sugars → starch and cellulose; amino acids → proteins; nucleotides → DNA. DNA and proteins are made from several different kinds of monomer, which allows them to carry information or have many different shapes, whereas starch and cellulose are made from just one kind of sugar monomer.

workedExamples.title: Matching polymers to monomers
workedExamples.question: Name the monomers that make up cellulose, proteins and DNA.
steps: Cellulose is a carbohydrate polymer: its monomers are sugars (glucose).
Proteins are made from amino acids.
workedExamples.answer: Cellulose: sugars; proteins: amino acids; DNA: nucleotides.

workedExamples.title: Describing the structure of DNA
workedExamples.question: Describe the structure of a DNA molecule.
steps: DNA is a polymer, so it is made of many monomers joined in chains.
The monomers are nucleotides, and there are four different ones.
Most DNA has two of these polymer chains, twisted together.
workedExamples.answer: Two polymer chains made from four different nucleotide monomers, in the form of a double helix.

workedExamples.title: Comparing starch and DNA
workedExamples.question: Give one similarity and one difference between starch and DNA.
steps: Similarity: both are naturally occurring polymers made of many monomers.
Difference in monomers: starch is made from one type of sugar monomer; DNA from four different nucleotides.
Difference in function: starch stores energy; DNA stores genetic information.
workedExamples.answer: Both are natural polymers; starch is made from sugars and stores energy, whereas DNA is made from four nucleotides and encodes genetic instructions.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think DNA is made from amino acids.
misconceptions.right: In fact DNA is made from nucleotides. Amino acids are the monomers of proteins; DNA carries the code for making proteins.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think starch and cellulose are made from different monomers.
misconceptions.right: In fact both are made from sugar (glucose) monomers; they differ in how the units are joined.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think DNA is a single chain.
misconceptions.right: In fact most DNA molecules are two polymer chains twisted together in a double helix.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think polymers are only plastics made from crude oil.
misconceptions.right: In fact living things make many natural polymers, including DNA, proteins, starch and cellulose.

realWorld: DNA profiling compares the order of nucleotides in DNA samples to identify people in forensic science.
Cotton clothing and paper are made mainly of cellulose from plants.
Potatoes, rice and bread provide starch, a major source of energy in our diet.
separateOnlyContent: All of this subtopic is for separate Chemistry (8462) only; Combined Science chemistry does not cover naturally occurring polymers.
examTips: Learn the three monomer to polymer pairs: sugars → starch and cellulose; amino acids → proteins; nucleotides → DNA.
When describing DNA, include: two polymer chains, four different nucleotide monomers, double helix.
State the function of DNA precisely: it encodes genetic instructions for the development and functioning of living organisms and viruses.
Do not mix up nucleotides (DNA) and amino acids (proteins).

questions.question: How many different nucleotide monomers are used to make DNA?

To carry oxygen in the blood

markScheme: 1 mark: proteins are made from amino acids; starch from sugars (glucose)
1 mark: proteins use many different amino acids, whereas starch uses one type of sugar monomer
questions.explanation: A comparison needs a point about each and a linking word such as 'whereas'.

questions.question: Describe the structure and function of DNA.
markScheme: Indicative content: DNA is deoxyribonucleic acid; large molecule; essential for life; encodes genetic instructions; for the development and functioning of living organisms and viruses; most DNA is two polymer chains; made from four different monomers called nucleotides; double helix.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): accurate description of both structure (two chains, nucleotides, double helix) and function (genetic instructions).
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements about either structure or function.
questions.explanation: A full answer covers both what DNA is made of and what it does.

questions.question:
Living organisms make several naturally occurring polymers.
Compare DNA, proteins, starch and cellulose.
In your answer, refer to:
• their monomers
• the variety of monomers used
• their roles.
markScheme: Indicative content: DNA: monomers are nucleotides; four different nucleotides; two chains in a double helix; encodes genetic instructions for development and functioning of organisms and viruses. Proteins: monomers are amino acids; many different amino acids combined in the same chain; roles such as enzymes, structural proteins, haemoglobin. Starch: monomers are sugars (glucose); one type of monomer; energy store in plants. Cellulose: monomers are sugars (glucose); one type of monomer; forms plant cell walls; starch and cellulose share the same monomer but differ in how units are joined; DNA and proteins use several different monomers whose order matters.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): correct monomers for all four, comparison of the variety of monomers, and a role for each, with clear comparisons.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): correct monomers for most polymers with some roles or comparisons.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): one or two correct monomer to polymer links.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Organise by feature and use comparative language: 'DNA uses four different monomers, whereas starch uses only one'.

questions.question:
Glucose is a sugar.
Which natural polymers are made from glucose monomers?
markScheme: 1 mark: starch and cellulose
questions.explanation: Glucose is a sugar; sugars are the monomers of starch and cellulose.

questions.question: Give the name of the shape formed by the two chains of a DNA molecule.
markScheme: 1 mark: double helix
questions.explanation: The two polymer chains twist around each other to form a double helix.

questions.question:
A student says:
'Proteins and DNA are both polymers, so they are made from the same monomers.'
Which response to the student is correct?
options: Correct: both are made from nucleotides
Correct: both are made from amino acids
Wrong: proteins are made from amino acids and DNA from nucleotides
Wrong: proteins are made from sugars and DNA from amino acids
markScheme: 1 mark: proteins from amino acids, DNA from nucleotides
questions.explanation: Being polymers does not mean sharing monomers. Each natural polymer has its own type of monomer.

questions.question: Give one use of starch in plants.
markScheme: 1 mark: energy store
questions.explanation: Plants store glucose as starch, for example in potatoes.

questions.question: Give one role of cellulose in plants.
markScheme: 1 mark: forms cell walls / gives strength or support
questions.explanation: Cellulose fibres make up plant cell walls.
